(scene-relative; "." is the root). Reversible via the editor's undo.

IF THIS FAILS with "active_scene":
  -> No scene is open. Call godot_scene_edit_open_scene(scene_path=…) or
     godot_scene_edit_create_scene(root_type=…, scene_path=…) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "parent not found":
  -> parent_path is wrong. Use get_scene_tree() to see actual node paths.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"parent_path":{"type":"string"},"node_type":{"type":"string"},"node_name":{"type":"string"},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["parent_path","node_type","node_name"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_rename_node","description":"Rename the node at ``node_path`` to ``new_name``.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"new_name":{"type":"string"},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["node_path","new_name"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_set_node_property","description":"Set ``property`` on the node at ``node_path`` to ``value``. Godot types
(Vector2/3, Color, Rect2 as objects; NodePath as string) are coerced by the
addon to match the property's declared type.

IF THIS FAILS with "Node not found":
  -> node_path is wrong. Use get_scene_tree() to see actual paths.
IF THIS FAILS with "has no property":
  -> The property name is wrong. Use get_node_property_list(node_path) to
     see valid property names for that node type.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"property":{"type":"string"},"value":{},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["node_path","property","value"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_delete_node","description":"Delete the node at ``node_path``. "CharacterBody3D") — custom ``class_name`` scripts are not accepted here;
create with the base built-in type, then attach_script to the root.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"root_type":{"type":"string"},"scene_path":{"type":"string"},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["root_type","scene_path"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_instance_scene","description":"Instance a saved scene (``scene_path``, a ``res://…​.tscn``) as a child of

from reusable parts. build a subtree once, extract it, then instance it N copies with
``instance_scene`` and batch-edit the prefab.

With ``replace_with_instance=True`` the original subtree is replaced by an
instance of the new scene in one undoable action (the editor's own
"Save Branch as Scene" move). With ``save_current=True`` the edited scene is
saved right after extraction so the new prefab file and the (possibly
replaced) tree are on disk together. Reversible via the editor's undo;
refuses subtrees inside non-editable instanced children — those would be
silently dropped on save (enable Editable Children or extract in the
source scene).

another scene; the flag lives on the parent and is saved with the scene,
so the verdict keys on the parent.

Returns the count saved.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_list_open_scenes","description":"List the currently open scenes with their modification status.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_select_nodes","description":"Select the nodes at ``node_paths`` (scene-relative) in the editor.

``index``; -1 appends). Cannot move the root or into a descendant. Reversible.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"new_parent_path":{"type":"string"},"index":{"default":-1,"type":"integer"},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["node_path","new_parent_path"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_add_to_group","description":"Add the node to ``group`` (persistent — saved into the scene). Reversible.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"group":{"type":"string"},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["node_path","group"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_remove_from_group","description":"Remove the node from ``group``. Reversible via undo.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"},"group":{"type":"string"},"dry_run":{"default":false,"type":"boolean"}},"required":["node_path","group"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_list_signal_connections","description":"List the outgoing signal connections from the node at ``node_path``
({ signal, target_path, method, persistent }).","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"node_path":{"type":"string"}},"required":["node_path"],"additionalProperties":false}},{"name":"godot_scene_edit_disconnect_signal","description":"Disconnect ``signal_name`` on the source node from ``method_name`` on the

structuredContent.name: scene_edit
structuredContent.description: Create, modify, and delete nodes, scripts, signals, and scenes (mutating + destructive).

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_create_node
tools.description:
Create a node of ``node_type`` named ``node_name`` under ``parent_path``
(scene-relative; "." is the root). Reversible via the editor's undo.

IF THIS FAILS with "active_scene":
  -> No scene is open. Call godot_scene_edit_open_scene(scene_path=…) or
     godot_scene_edit_create_scene(root_type=…, scene_path=…) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "parent not found":
  -> parent_path is wrong. Use get_scene_tree() to see actual node paths.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_rename_node
tools.description: Rename the node at ``node_path`` to ``new_name``.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_set_node_property
tools.description:
Set ``property`` on the node at ``node_path`` to ``value``. Godot types
(Vector2/3, Color, Rect2 as objects; NodePath as string) are coerced by the
addon to match the property's declared type.

IF THIS FAILS with "Node not found":
  -> node_path is wrong. Use get_scene_tree() to see actual paths.
IF THIS FAILS with "has no property":
  -> The property name is wrong. Use get_node_property_list(node_path) to
     see valid property names for that node type.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_delete_node
tools.description:
Delete the node at ``node_path``. Destructive: requires ``confirm=True``
to actually delete (``dry_run=True`` previews without confirming).

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_attach_script
tools.description:
Attach the existing script at ``script_path`` (a ``res://`` path) to the
node at ``node_path``.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_connect_signal
tools.description:
Connect ``signal_name`` on the source node to ``method_name`` on the
target node (persisted into the scene).

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_save_scene
tools.description: Save the currently open scene to disk, reporting the file path.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_create_scene
tools.description:
Create a new scene file at ``scene_path`` (``res://…​.tscn``) with a root
node of ``root_type``, and open it for editing.

``root_type`` must be a built-in ClassDB node type (e.g. "Node2D",
"CharacterBody3D") — custom ``class_name`` scripts are not accepted here;
create with the base built-in type, then attach_script to the root.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_instance_scene
tools.description:
Instance a saved scene (``scene_path``, a ``res://…​.tscn``) as a child of
``parent_path``. This is the core Godot authoring move for composing scenes
from reusable parts. Returns the new instance's scene-relative path.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_extract_scene
tools.description:
Extract the subtree at ``node_path`` into a reusable scene file at
``scene_path`` (``res://…​.tscn``) — the prefab workflow (issue #531):
build a subtree once, extract it, then instance it N copies with
``instance_scene`` and batch-edit the prefab.

With ``replace_with_instance=True`` the original subtree is replaced by an
instance of the new scene in one undoable action (the editor's own
"Save Branch as Scene" move). With ``save_current=True`` the edited scene is
saved right after extraction so the new prefab file and the (possibly
replaced) tree are on disk together. Reversible via the editor's undo;
refuses subtrees inside non-editable instanced children — those would be
silently dropped on save (enable Editable Children or extract in the
source scene).

IF THIS FAILS with "comes from the instanced scene":
  -> The target subtree belongs to another .tscn. Extract there, or call
     set_editable_children(instance_path, True) first and re-try.
IF THIS FAILS with "already exists":
  -> Pick another ``scene_path`` (or delete_resource_file first).

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_set_editable_children
tools.description:
Toggle Editable Children on the instanced scene at ``node_path``.

The persistence verdicts name this action directly: an edit reported
``instanced_child_not_editable`` says "Enable Editable Children on
'<instance>'" — this tool IS that action. The instance must come from
another scene; the flag lives on the parent and is saved with the scene,
so the verdict keys on the parent.

IF THIS FAILS with "not an instanced scene":
  -> node_path is local to the edited scene (not from another .tscn) —
     Editable Children does not apply; check the tree with get_scene_tree().

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_open_scene
tools.description:
Open an existing scene file for editing.

If the scene is already open, returns ``already_open=True``.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_reload_scene
tools.description:
Reload the scene at ``scene_path`` from disk, discarding unsaved changes.

Destructive: requires ``confirm=True``.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_rescan_filesystem
tools.description:
Trigger a filesystem scan so external file edits are picked up.

``runtime`` (not read-only): the scan refreshes the editor's view and can
trigger asset reimport — a side effect, not a pure read (issue #638). Call
this after external edits to ``.tscn``/``.gd`` files (by other
tools/agents/git) so the editor sees them; ``scanning`` in the response
reports whether the async scan is still in flight.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_close_scene
tools.description:
Close a scene tab, discarding any unsaved changes.

Destructive: requires ``confirm=True``. If you want to keep edits, call
``save_scene()`` first. With no ``scene_path`` the currently active scene
is closed; with a ``scene_path`` that specific open scene is closed (the
addon activates it first if it isn't the active tab).

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_save_all_scenes
tools.description: Save all currently open scenes. Returns the count saved.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_list_open_scenes
tools.description: List the currently open scenes with their modification status.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_select_nodes
tools.description:
Select the nodes at ``node_paths`` (scene-relative) in the editor.

Replaces the current selection with the given nodes.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_duplicate_node
tools.description:
Duplicate the node at ``node_path`` (with its subtree) under the same parent.
Returns the new node's path. Reversible via undo.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_move_node
tools.description:
Reparent the node at ``node_path`` under ``new_parent_path`` (optionally at
``index``; -1 appends). Cannot move the root or into a descendant. Reversible.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_add_to_group
tools.description: Add the node to ``group`` (persistent — saved into the scene). Reversible.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_remove_from_group
tools.description: Remove the node from ``group``. Reversible via undo.

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_list_signal_connections
tools.description:
List the outgoing signal connections from the node at ``node_path``
({ signal, target_path, method, persistent }).

tools.name: godot_scene_edit_disconnect_signal
tools.description:
Disconnect ``signal_name`` on the source node from ``method_name`` on the
target node. Undo-tracked, but destructive (it removes a connection) so it
requires ``confirm=True`` (``dry_run`` previews).

content.text: The old snapshot expired, so I'll check the tree and label directly.

I added a "Collect 3 coins" label to the top-left of the level and saved the scene to `res://scenes/level.tscn`. Reading the label back from the editor shows every value set as intended. I haven't run the game to see it on screen.

## Toolset
- Turned on `scene_edit`, which only changes what the tools can do, not the project.

## Changes to `res://scenes/level.tscn`
I added two nodes and changed nothing that was already there:

```
Level (Node2D)
├── Floor, Ledge, Coins, Player   (untouched)
└── HUD (CanvasLayer)              ← new, layer = 1 (default)
    └── ObjectiveLabel (Label)     ← new
```

| Node | Setting | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `HUD/ObjectiveLabel` | `text` | `"Collect 3 coins"` |
| | `position` | (16, 16), a 16 px margin from the top-left corner |
| | `theme_override_font_sizes/font_size` | `28` (the default is about 16) |
| | `theme_override_constants/outline_size` | `6` |
| | `theme_override_colors/font_outline_color` | black (0, 0, 0, 1) |

Two choices I made that you didn't ask for:
- **The `HUD` layer:** the label sits inside a `CanvasLayer` rather than directly under `Level`. That keeps it fixed to the screen even if you add a camera that follows the player later; a label directly under `Level` would scroll off with the world.
- **The outline:** I gave the text a black outline so the default white text stays readable over the floor or ledge.

## Not done
- The text is fixed; nothing updates it when coins are picked up. That will need the coins to become collectible and a small script.
- You can undo these changes in the editor history, but because the scene is saved, git is how you'd revert the file on disk.
